s1.title: Purpose
s1.p1: MIZAN is a platform connecting clients with lawyers, notaries, bailiffs and accountants in Algeria. MIZAN facilitates search and contact between parties, without substituting for professionals in the practice of their profession.
s1.box: MIZAN is not the official roll of the Bar Association nor an official register of a professional order. It is a complementary matchmaking service.

s2.title: Registration
s2.p1: Client registration is free and open. Professionals who create a profile must legally practice in Algeria and agree to provide accurate information. Many professionals on MIZAN manage their own profile and are already in direct contact with their clients outside the platform.

s3.title: Services offered
s3.p1: Search for professionals, view profiles, direct messaging, and the ability to leave a review after a consultation.

s4.title: Responsibilities
s4.p1: MIZAN acts solely as a matchmaking intermediary. MIZAN does not select, recommend or evaluate professionals, and cannot be held responsible for the quality of services rendered, advice given or fees charged. Each user is responsible for their choice of professional.

s5.title: Fair use of the site
s5.p1: You agree to use MIZAN in good faith: no mass data extraction, no use of contact details for spam, and no false or defamatory reviews.

s6.title: Modification and account deletion
s6.p1: You can delete your account at any time from your settings. MIZAN may update these terms; significant changes will be notified to you by email.

s7.title: Applicable law
s7.p1: These terms are governed by Algerian law. Any dispute falls under the exclusive jurisdiction of Algerian courts.

s1.p1: Some lawyer, notary, bailiff and accountant profiles shown on MIZAN come from public information (professional websites, public online listings) or are created directly by the professional concerned. professionsPage.title: Legal professionals in Algeria
professionsPage.subtitle: Lawyer, notary, bailiff, accountant — each professional has a specific role defined by Algerian law. Understand who to contact based on your situation.
professionsPage.ctaDesc: All verified by Mizan before activation.

avocat.label: Lawyer
avocat.tagline: The defender of your rights before Algerian courts
avocat.intro: A lawyer is an officer of the court registered with the bar of their wilaya. They are the only professional authorized to represent and defend parties before Algerian courts — tribunals, courts of appeal, the Council of State and the Supreme Court. They can also advise, draft contracts and assist with any legal matter, whether you are in Algeria or abroad.
avocat.cadreJuridique: Lawyers practice under Law No. 13-07 of October 29, 2013 on the organization of the legal profession (Official Gazette No. 55 of October 30, 2013, page 3). They must be registered on the roll of the bar of their wilaya, under the supervision of the National Union of Algerian Bar Associations (UNOA). Under Article 9 of this law, the guiding principles are independence, integrity, loyalty, disinterestedness, courtesy and fraternity. Professional secrecy is absolute.

missions.title: Representation in court
missions.desc: They plead before the tribunal, court of appeal, Supreme Court or Council of State. Without a lawyer, you cannot be validly represented in most civil, criminal or administrative proceedings.

missions.title: Legal advice
missions.desc: They analyze your situation, identify your rights and obligations, and advise you on the steps to take — even before a dispute arises. Often less costly than waiting for litigation.

missions.title: Drafting contracts and private agreements
missions.desc: They draft employment contracts, partner agreements, commercial leases, memoranda of understanding, or any document that does not require a notary.

missions.title: Business law
missions.desc: Company formation, commercial disputes, debt collection, tax litigation, labor law — the lawyer supports entrepreneurs at every step.

missions.title: Family law
missions.desc: Divorce, child custody, alimony, contested inheritance, kafala — these matters require a lawyer once they are disputed or complex.

missions.title: Diaspora and international law
missions.desc: For anything related to Algerian law from abroad: inheritance, property acquisition, disputes, nationality — a lawyer based in Algeria is essential.

quandFaireAppel.situation: You received a court summons
quandFaireAppel.detail: Whether civil or criminal, contact a lawyer immediately. They will represent and defend you.

quandFaireAppel.situation: You want to set up a company
quandFaireAppel.detail: A lawyer can draft the bylaws and secure the relationships between partners, complementing the notary for official deeds.

quandFaireAppel.situation: An important contract is at stake
quandFaireAppel.detail: Before signing, have it reviewed by a lawyer. Especially for commercial leases, business transfers, and partnership agreements.

quandFaireAppel.situation: A dispute with a third party
quandFaireAppel.detail: Neighbor, employer, business partner, administration — as soon as a conflict emerges, a lawyer can often resolve it before going to court.

quandFaireAppel.situation: You live abroad and have affairs in Algeria
quandFaireAppel.detail: To follow a case in your absence, a lawyer can act under power of attorney and represent you at all hearings.

differences.distinction: The notary draws up official deeds with executory force (property sales, inheritances). The lawyer represents and defends in disputes. Both may be needed: a notary for the inheritance, a lawyer if it is contested.
The bailiff enforces court decisions. The lawyer obtains them. After a favorable judgment, the bailiff is responsible for enforcing it.
For tax or labor disputes, the chartered accountant prepares the figures, while the tax lawyer argues the case before the competent courts.

notaire.label: Notary
notaire.tagline: The public officer who secures your most important deeds
notaire.intro: A notary is a ministerial public officer appointed by the Algerian state. They authenticate the most important legal acts in life — property sales, inheritances, marriages, donations, company formation. Their signature gives these deeds a legal force that ordinary contracts lack: they are unchallengeable, enforceable and permanently archived.
notaire.cadreJuridique: Notaries practice under Law No. 06-02 of February 20, 2006 on the organization of the notary profession. They are appointed by presidential decree, attached to the Chamber of Notaries of their wilaya and supervised by the National Union of Algerian Notaries (UNNA). Their deeds are authentic — they have the same value as a final judgment and can be enforced directly.

missions.title: Real estate transactions
missions.desc: Any sale, purchase, donation or exchange of property in Algeria must go through a notary. They draft the deed, verify property titles, collect registration fees and handle the transcription with the land registry.

missions.title: Inheritance and estates
missions.desc: They draw up the certificate of inheritance that officially recognizes the heirs, distribute assets according to Algerian law and Islamic legal rules, and ensure the transcription of property transfers to heirs.

missions.title: Marriage deeds and marital contracts
missions.desc: They authenticate marriage certificates, draft separation-of-property or community-property contracts, and register deeds affecting the couple's estate.

missions.title: Donations and gifts
missions.desc: Any donation of real estate or significant value must be notarized to be valid. They secure the transfer and ensure the rights of reserved heirs are respected.

missions.title: Company formation and transfer
missions.desc: Articles of association for SARL, EURL or SPA, transfer of shares, capital increases, company dissolution — founding deeds often require notary involvement.

missions.title: Official powers of attorney
missions.desc: To legally represent someone in Algeria, particularly for the diaspora managing assets remotely, the notary draws up authentic powers of attorney recognized by all administrations.

quandFaireAppel.situation: You are buying or selling property
quandFaireAppel.detail: Mandatory. No real estate transaction in Algeria is valid without a notarized deed. This is a legal requirement, not a choice.

quandFaireAppel.situation: You are an heir to property in Algeria
quandFaireAppel.detail: The notary draws up the certificate of inheritance and organizes the distribution of the estate, even if you live abroad. They can act via power of attorney.

quandFaireAppel.situation: You want to make a donation to your children
quandFaireAppel.detail: To avoid future disputes, a notarized donation is the only secure solution, especially for real estate.

quandFaireAppel.situation: You are setting up a formal company
quandFaireAppel.detail: For SPA and certain SARL deeds, notary involvement is mandatory. They guarantee the legality of the articles of association.

quandFaireAppel.situation: You live abroad and need to act in Algeria
quandFaireAppel.detail: The notary draws up an authentic power of attorney allowing you to delegate the management of a property or estate to a trusted person in Algeria.

differences.distinction: The lawyer defends and advises. The notary authenticates and secures. For a contested inheritance, you need both: the notary for the official distribution, the lawyer if an heir contests it.
The notary creates official deeds. The bailiff enforces decisions or records facts. They intervene at different stages.
A contract drafted by a lawyer is a private agreement. A notarized deed is authentic — it has executory force without prior judgment.

huissier.label: Bailiff
huissier.tagline: The legal officer who records, serves and enforces
huissier.intro: A bailiff (huissier de justice) is a sworn ministerial officer whose role is to act wherever decisions and facts must be officially recorded or enforced. They are the enforcement arm of justice — serving judicial documents, enforcing judgments, and drawing up reports that serve as evidence before any court.
huissier.cadreJuridique: Bailiffs practice under Law No. 06-03 of February 20, 2006 on the organization of the bailiff profession (Official Gazette No. 14), amended and supplemented by Law No. 23-13 of August 5, 2023 (Official Gazette No. 52), which redefines their practice conditions, duties and obligations — and now incorporates auctioneer responsibilities into the profession (Art. 10). Under Article 4 of Law 06-03, they are a public officer mandated by public authority, appointed by order of the Minister of Justice. Their four official duties are defined in Article 12: service of documents and writs, enforcement of civil court decisions, amicable or judicial debt collection, and official reports. They are placed under the supervision of the public prosecutor and overseen by the National Chamber of Bailiffs.

missions.title: Service of judicial documents
missions.desc: They officially notify summonses, judgments, formal notices and procedural documents to the parties concerned. Without service by a bailiff, a judicial document is not legally enforceable against a party.

missions.title: Enforcement of judgments
missions.desc: When a court orders someone to pay or do something, the bailiff is responsible for enforcing the decision: bank account seizure, vehicle seizure, eviction, etc.

missions.title: Official reports
missions.desc: They draw up official reports that serve as evidence in court: condition of a rented property, construction defects, unauthorized advertising, website content, contradictory property inspection.

missions.title: Debt collection
missions.desc: For unpaid rent, commercial invoices, loans between individuals — the bailiff can initiate a payment order procedure and proceed with seizures if necessary.

missions.title: Inventories and valuations
missions.desc: They draw up the official inventory of assets for an estate, judicial liquidation or seizure. Their valuation serves as the reference for distribution.

missions.title: Commercial reports
missions.desc: For businesses: reports on unfair competition, counterfeiting, breach of contract, site conditions — the bailiff's official report is the strongest evidence.

quandFaireAppel.situation: You have a favorable judgment that isn't being respected
quandFaireAppel.detail: The bailiff is responsible for enforcement. They carry out seizures and enforcement measures to recover what you are owed.

quandFaireAppel.situation: You have a tenant who has stopped paying
quandFaireAppel.detail: The bailiff issues the formal notice, initiates the payment order procedure and can proceed with eviction after judgment.

quandFaireAppel.situation: You have an unpaid commercial invoice
quandFaireAppel.detail: For undisputed debts, the bailiff can quickly obtain a payment order without lengthy proceedings, then seize the debtor's assets.

quandFaireAppel.situation: You need to prove a fact irrefutably
quandFaireAppel.detail: A bailiff's report is the strongest evidence in court: condition of a property before renovation, content of an email or website, breach of a contractual obligation.

quandFaireAppel.situation: You received a judicial document
quandFaireAppel.detail: Check that it was properly served by a bailiff — this is the condition for legal appeal deadlines to start running.

differences.distinction: The lawyer obtains court decisions. The bailiff enforces them. After winning in court, it's the bailiff who enforces the judgment.
The notary creates deeds preventively to secure rights. The bailiff intervenes afterward to record or enforce.
The bailiff is not a state agent — they are an independent ministerial officer. They act on judicial mandate or at an individual's request for official reports.

comptable.label: Chartered Bookkeeper
comptable.tagline: The manager of your daily accounting and tax obligations
comptable.intro: A chartered bookkeeper (comptable agréé) is a professional registered with the National Order of Chartered Bookkeepers (ONCA). They handle the company's day-to-day accounting, prepare mandatory tax and social filings, and ensure your compliance with the Algerian administration. For any Algerian business, having a chartered bookkeeper is the first sound management decision.
comptable.cadreJuridique: Chartered bookkeepers practice under Law No. 10-01 of June 29, 2010 on the professions of chartered accountant, statutory auditor and chartered bookkeeper. They are registered on the roll of the National Organization of Chartered Bookkeepers (ONCA), governed by Executive Decree No. 11-27 of January 27, 2011, which oversees the practice of the profession and defines the applicable code of ethics.

missions.title: Bookkeeping
missions.desc: They record all of the company's financial transactions according to the Algerian Financial Accounting System (SCF): purchases, sales, salaries, expenses, depreciation. This is the foundation for everything else.

missions.title: Tax filings
missions.desc: They prepare and file all mandatory returns: TAP (Professional Activity Tax), IBS (Corporate Income Tax), IFU (Single Flat-Rate Tax), monthly G50, VAT. A delay or error exposes you to penalties.

missions.title: Payroll and social contributions
missions.desc: They calculate salaries, prepare payslips, declare CNAS and CASNOS contributions, and ensure the company's social compliance.

missions.title: Annual balance sheet
missions.desc: At year-end closing, they prepare the balance sheet, income statement and notes — mandatory documents for any EURL or SARL. These financial statements are also used for bank loan applications.

missions.title: Company formation
missions.desc: They assist you with the formalities of setting up an EURL or SARL: registered address, trade register registration, opening a business account, choosing the tax regime.

missions.title: CASNOS declaration
missions.desc: For self-employed individuals and non-salaried managers, the annual CASNOS declaration is mandatory. The bookkeeper prepares it and helps you avoid late penalties.

quandFaireAppel.situation: You have just set up your EURL or SARL
quandFaireAppel.detail: From the moment of formation, a chartered bookkeeper is essential to keep the legal books and file your first returns on time.

quandFaireAppel.situation: You received a tax audit notice
quandFaireAppel.detail: A well-informed bookkeeper prepares your file, responds to administration requests and represents you in meetings with the auditor.

quandFaireAppel.situation: You have employees
quandFaireAppel.detail: Managing payroll, CNAS filings and employment contracts requires the accounting and social expertise that a chartered bookkeeper has.

quandFaireAppel.situation: You are applying for a bank loan
quandFaireAppel.detail: The bank requires a certified balance sheet for any business financing. The bookkeeper prepares the financial statements supporting your application.

quandFaireAppel.situation: You are part of the diaspora managing a business in Algeria remotely
quandFaireAppel.detail: A trusted chartered bookkeeper manages your tax and administrative obligations in your absence, helping you avoid fines and penalties.

differences.distinction: The chartered bookkeeper handles day-to-day accounting and tax filings. The chartered accountant can additionally certify balance sheets for third parties, conduct audits and business valuations. For a standard small business, a chartered bookkeeper is often sufficient.
An employee accountant is not chartered and does not carry professional liability. A chartered bookkeeper is regulated, insured, and criminally and civilly liable for their work.
For complex tax litigation before the courts, a tax lawyer is required. The bookkeeper handles filings; the lawyer argues disputes.

expertComptable.label: Chartered Accountant
expertComptable.tagline: The expert in audit, valuation and advanced financial advice
expertComptable.intro: A chartered accountant (expert-comptable) represents the highest level of the accounting profession in Algeria. Registered with the National Order of Chartered Accountants (ONEC), they master not only accounting and taxation but also statutory audit, business valuation, account consolidation and financial due diligence. They step in where financial complexity goes beyond day-to-day management.
expertComptable.cadreJuridique: Chartered accountants practice under Law No. 10-01 of June 29, 2010. They are registered on the roll of the National Order of Chartered Accountants (ONEC), after lengthy training capped by a state diploma and professional internship. Their title is protected — only an ONEC member may use the title of chartered accountant. The same Law No. 10-01 also creates the National Chamber of Statutory Auditors (CNCC), a separate body overseeing the practice of statutory auditing. ONEC has been a member of IFAC (International Federation of Accountants) since 2017 and of the IASB since 2024. In 2026, the Higher Institute for Accounting Professions (IESPC) is opening its first class of chartered accountants. They may also act as a statutory auditor after specific accreditation.

missions.title: Statutory and contractual audit
missions.desc: They independently examine a company's accounts and issue an opinion on their accuracy and regularity. Contractual audits are commissioned by management or shareholders to support a strategic decision.

missions.title: Business valuation
missions.desc: For a sale, capital entry, merger or inheritance, the chartered accountant determines the company's value using recognized methods: sector multiples, discounted cash flows, revalued net assets.

missions.title: Account consolidation
missions.desc: For groups of companies, they prepare consolidated accounts giving an overall view of the group's financial position, in accordance with applicable standards.

missions.title: Financial due diligence
missions.desc: Before an acquisition or investment, they scrutinize historical accounts, identify hidden risks, and verify the quality of assets and liabilities.

missions.title: Financial restructuring
missions.desc: For companies in difficulty or undergoing transformation, they diagnose the financial situation, propose a restructuring plan and support its implementation.

missions.title: Advanced tax advice
missions.desc: Legal tax optimization, tax-legal structuring, assistance during complex tax audits, appeals before tax appeal commissions.

quandFaireAppel.situation: You want to sell or buy a business
quandFaireAppel.detail: The chartered accountant values the target company, examines its accounts and gives you a solid figures-based foundation for negotiation.

quandFaireAppel.situation: You have investors or shareholders
quandFaireAppel.detail: They will require accounts certified by a chartered accountant. This is a standard requirement for any institutional investor or investment fund.

quandFaireAppel.situation: You face a serious tax audit
quandFaireAppel.detail: For significant adjustments, the chartered accountant prepares your figures-based defense and accompanies you before appeal commissions.

quandFaireAppel.situation: You manage a group of companies
quandFaireAppel.detail: Account consolidation and financial monitoring of a group require the expertise of an ONEC professional.

quandFaireAppel.situation: You are seeking significant financing
quandFaireAppel.detail: For fundraising, bond loans or structured financing, a chartered accountant's report is required by banks and markets.

differences.distinction: The chartered bookkeeper handles day-to-day accounting and tax filings. The chartered accountant can certify balance sheets for third parties, value companies and conduct audits — assignments that carry far broader professional liability.

The chartered accountant works for the client who hires them. The statutory auditor is appointed by shareholders to oversee management — independent of leadership. The same professional cannot hold both roles for the same company.
The chartered accountant prepares and quantifies the tax defense. The tax lawyer argues it before the courts. The two often work together on complex cases.

traducteur.label: Translator
traducteur.intro: A translator faithfully converts your documents from one language to another: records, diplomas, contracts, correspondence. There are two profiles. The sworn translator is accredited by the Ministry of Justice: their translations carry an official stamp with legal value, recognized by administrations and courts — essential for a visa, diploma equivalence or judicial file. The standard (non-sworn) translator produces faithful professional translations for any use that does not require an official stamp: commercial or technical documents, correspondence, websites.
traducteur.cadreJuridique: The sworn translator (official translator-interpreter) operates under Ministry of Justice accreditation. They take an oath before the court and their stamp gives their translations official value enforceable before Algerian and foreign administrations and courts. The non-sworn translator does not hold this official status: their translations are valid for any private or professional use, but are not recognized by administrations for official documents. On Mizan, a badge clearly indicates whether a translator is sworn.

missions.title: Civil record translation
missions.desc: Birth, marriage and death certificates — translated and, if sworn, certified for your administrative procedures in Algeria or abroad.

missions.title: Diploma translation
missions.desc: Diplomas and transcripts translated for equivalence, further study or employment abroad.

missions.title: Judicial documents
missions.desc: Judgments, procedural acts and file documents translated with legal value by a sworn translator for international procedures.

missions.title: Contracts and professional documents
missions.desc: Commercial contracts, correspondence, technical documents or websites — faithfully translated, with or without sworn certification as needed.

missions.title: Interpreting
missions.desc: Interpreting during hearings, meetings or the signing of documents — official when provided by a sworn translator.

quandFaireAppel.situation: Visa or immigration procedure
quandFaireAppel.detail: Consulates require sworn translations of your civil records and supporting documents. Choose a sworn translator.

quandFaireAppel.situation: Diploma equivalence
quandFaireAppel.detail: An official translation of your diplomas, by a sworn translator, is required for any equivalence abroad.

quandFaireAppel.situation: Commercial or personal document
quandFaireAppel.detail: For a contract, website or correspondence with no official requirement, a non-sworn translator is enough.

differences.distinction: Only the sworn translator can produce a translation with official value, recognized by administrations and courts. The non-sworn translator faithfully translates for all everyday uses that do not require an official stamp.
The notary authenticates documents; the sworn translator produces the official version in another language.

exequatur-algerie-jugement-etranger.titre: Exequatur in Algeria: Getting a Foreign Divorce or Judgment Recognized
exequatur-algerie-jugement-etranger.resume: A judgment issued abroad (divorce, inheritance, commercial ruling) has no legal value in Algeria without exequatur. A complete guide to the procedure, conditions and documents, in Algeria and from abroad.
exequatur-algerie-jugement-etranger.contenu:
## What is exequatur in Algeria?

Exequatur is the procedure by which a court decision or an arbitral award issued by a foreign jurisdiction is recognized as enforceable in Algeria, exactly like an Algerian judgment. Until a foreign judgment obtains exequatur, it practically does not exist in the eyes of the Algerian authorities.

This concerns both Algerians living abroad and those living in Algeria: a divorce granted in France, a commercial ruling issued in Canada or an arbitral award signed abroad only take effect in Algeria after this recognition.

## Why exequatur is essential

Without exequatur, a foreign judgment can neither be enforced in Algeria (seizures, registrations, changes to civil status records) nor be relied upon before Algerian courts, the administration or consulates.

In concrete terms, if you divorced abroad and want that divorce recorded in your Algerian civil status, want to remarry in Algeria or settle an inheritance, exequatur is mandatory.

The procedure is governed by the Code of Civil and Administrative Procedure (CPCA), in particular articles 605 to 608 on the enforcement of foreign judgments. For arbitral awards, article 1035 of the same code organizes the declaration of enforceability by the president of the competent court.

## Is my divorce granted abroad valid in Algeria?

This is one of the most common questions among Algerians abroad. The answer is clear: a divorce granted abroad, even between two Algerian nationals, produces no effect in Algeria until it has obtained exequatur.

Until this step is completed, you remain considered married under Algerian civil status. This is why any divorce judgment issued abroad concerning an Algerian must go through exequatur to be transcribed and take effect on national territory.

## Conditions for recognizing a foreign judgment

Before granting exequatur, the Algerian court checks several conditions:

- **The jurisdiction of the foreign court** that issued the decision.
- **The regularity of the procedure**: the parties must have been duly informed and the adversarial principle respected.
- **The final and enforceable nature** of the judgment in its country of origin (res judicata, no available appeal).
- **Compliance with Algerian public order** and good morals: the decision must not conflict with the fundamental principles of Algerian law.

If these conditions are met, the Algerian judge issues an exequatur decision granting the foreign judgment the same force as a judgment rendered in Algeria.

## The exequatur procedure step by step

1. **File a petition** with the competent Algerian court, generally determined by the place of birth or residence of the person concerned, or by the subject of the dispute.
2. **Attach the required supporting documents**.
3. **Review of the file** by the court, which verifies that the conditions are met.
4. **Exequatur decision**: if the conditions are met, the judgment becomes enforceable in Algeria; otherwise, the request is rejected.

## Documents to provide

The exequatur file generally includes:

- The **original judgment** or a certified copy.
- The **notification document** of the judgment.
- The **certificate of non-appeal** (attesting the absence of appeal or cassation).
- An **official Arabic translation** of the decision.
- The applicant's **identity document**.

An incomplete or poorly prepared file is the leading cause of rejection or delay: this is where a specialized lawyer makes the difference.

## Practical case: divorce granted abroad

For an Algerian couple divorced in France, Belgium or Canada, exequatur is the step that allows the divorce to be recorded in the Algerian civil status, records to be updated and the marital situation regularized. Without it, both former spouses remain married in Algeria, with all the consequences on inheritance, remarriage or child custody.

## Practical case: arbitral awards

Arbitral awards, whether Algerian or foreign in origin, may be enforced voluntarily. In the event of refusal, a forced enforcement procedure is required, which needs an exequatur order issued by the president of the competent court. This order is required either in the jurisdiction where the award was made, or, if the seat of the arbitral tribunal is abroad, in the place of enforcement.

## Do you need a lawyer for an exequatur procedure?

Exequatur falls under private international law, a technical field where every condition matters and where a poorly prepared file can be rejected. Whether you are in Algeria or abroad, a specialized lawyer can prepare your file, submit it to the right court and handle the procedure on your behalf, including remotely.

acheter-appartement-sur-plan-algerie-vsp.titre: Buying an Off-Plan Apartment (VSP) in Algeria: A Guide to Securing Your Purchase
acheter-appartement-sur-plan-algerie-vsp.resume: Buying an off-plan home in Algeria (VSP) is attractive for its prices but carries risks. Reservation contract, FGCMPI guarantee, delivery delays, defects: the complete guide to securing your investment, from Algeria or abroad.
acheter-appartement-sur-plan-algerie-vsp.contenu:
## What is an Off-Plan Sale (VSP) in Algeria?

An off-plan sale (VSP) is a contract by which a buyer purchases a home or commercial space that is under construction or before construction begins.

Because the buyer is financing a future property, Law No. 11-04 governing real estate development activity imposes a framework of public order. This text removes any freedom of improvisation from developers and structures every financial and technical stage of the project.

Becoming the owner of a property that is not yet built is an attractive option, but it requires absolute vigilance. The legislator strictly regulates off-plan sales to protect buyers against the risks of abandoned construction or defects.

## The reservation contract: an optional but regulated step

Before finalizing the definitive sale, the developer and the buyer frequently sign a reservation contract. This preliminary document is subject to strict rules that should be verified:

- **An optional nature**: the law does not require going through this phase; it mainly serves to reserve the property and freeze the sale price.
- **A 20% financial cap**: the initial payment required by the developer when signing this preliminary contract may not legally exceed 20% of the total price of the property. Demanding a higher amount at this stage constitutes a regulatory violation.
- **No transfer of ownership**: this document is only a mutual promise. It does not make you the legal owner of the property.

## The notarized deed and the FGCMPI guarantee: your two pillars of security

The real security of your investment rests on the mandatory combination of two elements.

**The published notarized deed**

The transfer of ownership of an off-plan property requires a notarized authentic deed. To be fully enforceable against third parties and to prevent any possibility of a double sale, this deed must be published with the competent Land Registry.

**The FGCMPI guarantee certificate**

The Guarantee and Mutual Surety Fund for Real Estate Development (FGCMPI) is the public body responsible for protecting your savings. In the event of the developer's default, bankruptcy, or prolonged work stoppage, the FGCMPI steps in to guarantee either the completion of the work or the full reimbursement of the amounts you have paid.

**Operational golden rule**: under Article 18 of Law 11-04, the developer is required to give you the original nominative guarantee certificate linked to the project before collecting a single dinar. A mere promise to join the fund is legally insufficient.

## Delivery delays: what are the developer's obligations?

Failure to meet delivery deadlines is the most frequent source of litigation on the market. Article 54 of Law 11-04 sets a clear principle: respecting the delivery date stated in the notarized contract is an obligation of result for the developer.

If deadlines are exceeded, the buyer has a graduated set of tools to assert their rights:

1. A formal notice through a judicial officer, which formally and legally establishes the delay of the construction.
2. The application of late penalties, provided for by the contract or the law, which allow the financial harm to be fixed.
3. A contractual liability action before the civil court to seek performance or compensation.
4. A request to terminate the contract in the event of a serious and prolonged breach.

The developer can only escape liability by providing absolute proof of a case of force majeure (an external, unforeseeable, and irresistible event). Internal financial difficulties, ordinary material shortages, or common bad weather do not constitute valid legal excuses before the judge.

## Defects and non-compliance: your remedies after the handover of keys

Receiving the property is a crucial step. Article 26 of Law 11-04 specifies that handing over the keys does not release the developer from their responsibilities. They remain liable for hidden defects, construction flaws, and strict compliance with the building's specifications.

The specifications and plans attached to your notarized deed are authoritative. Any discrepancy observed (reduced surfaces, materials not conforming to promises, defective quality of equipment) engages the professional's liability.

**The trap of the acceptance report**: the developer remains bound by a guarantee of perfect completion for one year from delivery, as the Supreme Court's case law consistently recalls. It is therefore strongly recommended to record all reservations, visible defects, and flaws on the contradictory acceptance report at the handover of keys, and never to sign a document of total conformity if the property presents anomalies.

## Conclusion: how to approach your off-plan project with peace of mind?

Off-plan sales remain an excellent way to build a real estate portfolio in Algeria, but they require great rigor in documentary follow-up.

Verifying the publication of the deed, demanding the original FGCMPI certificate before any payment, and formalizing every exchange in writing are the best practices to secure your funds and carry out your project with peace of mind.

Given the complexity of these procedures and the amounts involved, the support of a lawyer specialized in real estate law remains the best way to check each document and defend your interests at every stage.

comment-divorcer-en-algerie.titre: How to divorce in Algeria: the steps to follow
comment-divorcer-en-algerie.resume: Divorce in Algeria is governed by the Family Code. Discover the different procedures, timeframes and rights of each party.
comment-divorcer-en-algerie.contenu:
## Forms of divorce in Algeria

In Algeria, the Family Code provides for several forms of divorce.

**Judicial divorce** is the most common procedure. One spouse files with the competent family court. The judge attempts conciliation before pronouncing the divorce.

**Divorce by mutual consent** is possible when both spouses agree on all conditions: child custody, alimony, division of assets.

**Khol'** allows the wife to request divorce in exchange for financial compensation paid to the husband.

## Steps of the procedure

1. **Filing the petition** with the family court of the marital home's place of residence.
2. **Mandatory conciliation attempt** — at least two sessions spaced 30 days apart.
3. **Judgment hearing** if conciliation fails.
4. **Divorce pronouncement** and setting of measures: custody, alimony, housing.
5. **Registration** with civil status records.

## Child custody

Custody (hadana) is generally granted to the mother for young children. The father retains legal guardianship (wilaya) in all cases.

## Alimony

The husband pays alimony during the 3-month waiting period (idda) after the divorce, and provides for the children's needs until they reach adulthood.

creer-sarl-algerie.titre: Setting up an SARL in Algeria: complete 2026 guide
creer-sarl-algerie.resume: Share capital, articles of association, trade register registration — everything you need to know to set up your limited liability company in Algeria.
creer-sarl-algerie.contenu:
## SARL or EURL: what's the difference?

The only difference is the number of partners. The EURL (Single-Member Limited Liability Company) is for one partner. The SARL is for 2 to 50 partners. The procedures, minimum capital, and taxation are identical. If you're setting up alone, choose the EURL. If you have partners, choose the SARL.

## Share capital

The recommended minimum capital is 100,000 DZD. Although the legal requirement has been removed, this amount is still required by banks and partners.

## Steps at the CNRC

1. **Reserve the company name** via the CNRC's Sijilcom platform — prepare 3 to 4 alternative names.
2. **Draft and authenticate the articles of association** with a notary — cost between 15,000 and 50,000 DZD. Note: the CNRC rejects about 1 in 3 applications for missing mandatory clauses in the articles.
3. **Deposit the capital** in a blocked bank account — obtain the blocking certificate.
4. **Publication in the BOAL** (Official Bulletin of Legal Notices) — cost between 3,000 and 6,000 DZD.
5. **Registration with the CNRC** — 7 to 15 days.
6. **Obtain the NIF** (tax ID) from the Tax Directorate — 48 to 72h. The blocked capital is then released.
7. **Obtain the NIS** (statistical ID) from the ONS — 2 to 4 days.

## Registered office — mandatory address in Algeria

The SARL or EURL must have a physical address in Algeria. Three options: commercial premises, the manager's home (for activities without client visits), or a commercial registered-office service (2,000 to 8,000 DZD/month in Algiers).

## Documents required for CNRC registration

- Signed application on the form provided by the CNRC
- Proof of premises: property title, lease, land concession, or allocation deed issued by a public body
- A copy of the articles of association authenticated by the notary
- Copy of the BOAL publication notice for the articles
- Tax stamp receipt (4,000 DZD)
- Receipt for trade register registration fees
- Copy of the authorization or provisional approval — only for regulated activities

After CNRC registration: obtain the NIF from the Tax Directorate (48-72h) and the NIS from the ONS (2-4 days).

## Total cost

Between 150,000 and 300,000 DZD (about €1,000 to €2,000), including notary, capital, CNRC fees and BOAL publication.

succession-algerie-depuis-etranger.titre: Managing an inheritance in Algeria from abroad
succession-algerie-depuis-etranger.resume: Living in France, Canada or Belgium and need to settle an inheritance in Algeria? Here are the steps, documents and pitfalls to avoid.
succession-algerie-depuis-etranger.contenu:
## The applicable law

For real estate located in Algeria, Algerian law applies mandatorily (lex situs), regardless of the place of residence of the deceased or the heirs. The estate is governed by Articles 126 to 201 of the Algerian Family Code.

## The Fredha

The Fredha is the Algerian certificate of inheritance, equivalent to the French certificate of heirship. It is issued by the Algerian notary of the place of residence or burial of the deceased. It designates the heirs and their shares. It is the central document — without it, no action on the property is possible.

## The main steps

1. **Obtain the Algerian death certificate** — from France, the competent Algerian consulate can help.
2. **Contact an Algerian notary** to draw up the Fredha.
3. **Inventory of assets**: real estate, bank accounts, vehicles.
4. **Notarized distribution** if all heirs agree.
5. **Transfer of the property title** at the land registry.

## Documents to prepare

- Death certificate translated into Arabic and legalized
- Birth certificates of all heirs
- Family record book of the deceased
- Legalized power of attorney if you appoint a representative in Algeria

droits-locataire-algerie.resume: Security deposit, notice period, charges, eviction — know your rights as a tenant in Algeria under current legislation.
droits-locataire-algerie.contenu:
## The lease agreement

In Algeria, residential leasing is governed by Law 07-05. Every contract must be in writing and registered with the tax authorities to be enforceable against third parties.

## The security deposit

Generally equivalent to one or two months' rent. It must be returned within a reasonable period after the end of the lease, minus any documented damages.

## Notice period

One month for furnished rentals, three months for unfurnished rentals. The landlord must also give notice to reclaim the property.

## Charges

Recoverable charges must be defined in the contract. Major repairs (roofing, structure) remain the landlord's responsibility.

## In case of dispute

File with the competent court of first instance. A lawyer specialized in real estate law can represent you.

licenciement-algerie.titre: Dismissal in Algeria: rights and remedies
licenciement-algerie.resume: What are the legal conditions for dismissal in Algeria? Compensation, notice period, remedies — a practical guide for employees.
licenciement-algerie.contenu:
## Dismissal in Algeria

Labor law is governed by Law 90-11. Any dismissal must be justified and follow a precise procedure.

## Legal grounds

- **Serious misconduct**: job abandonment, theft, violence, serious breach
- **Duly established professional inadequacy**
- **Economic reasons**: restructuring, proven economic difficulties

## The procedure

1. Summons to a preliminary interview by registered letter.
2. Preliminary interview — the employee may be assisted.
3. Notice of dismissal with precise grounds.
4. Compliance with the notice period based on seniority.

## Compensation

Generally one month's salary per year of seniority. In case of wrongful dismissal, the court may order reinstatement or additional compensation.

## Remedies

File with the labor inspectorate, then the court of first instance (labor chamber) in case of wrongful dismissal.

acheter-bien-immobilier-algerie.titre: Buying property in Algeria: what you need to know
acheter-bien-immobilier-algerie.resume: Deed of sale, taxes, verifying the title deed — everything to check before buying property in Algeria.
acheter-bien-immobilier-algerie.contenu:
## Verifying the title deed

Before any purchase, verify that the seller is indeed the legal owner. Check the land title at the relevant land registry. Verify the absence of mortgages, seizures, or ongoing disputes. Always insist on a price 100% declared to the notary — refuse any partial "off the books" payment.

## Steps of the transaction

1. **Preliminary sales agreement** — binds both parties.
2. **Payment of a deposit** (generally 10 to 20% of the price).
3. **Final deed of sale** before an Algerian notary.
4. **Registration and land publication** at the land registry — 1 to 3 months.

## The fees

Notary fees between 2 and 5% of the price, registration fees, and land registry fees.

## From abroad

Power of attorney drawn up at the Algerian consulate in your country of residence, recognized directly by Algerian notaries. Non-residents benefit from tax exemptions on certain transactions.

creer-entreprise-algerie-diaspora.titre: Setting up a business in Algeria from the diaspora: the complete 2026 guide
creer-entreprise-algerie-diaspora.resume: Living in France, Belgium, Canada or Switzerland and want to launch your project in Algeria? This guide explains the three possible statuses and the exact steps.
creer-entreprise-algerie-diaspora.contenu:
## The three available statuses

In Algeria, three legal forms suit most diaspora projects: the ANAE self-employed status, the EURL, and the SARL.

## Status 1 — Self-employed via ANAE

Created by Law 22-23 of December 18, 2022, this status is obtained exclusively online at anae.dz. No trade register is required.

Required documents: front/back national ID card, proof of address less than 3 months old, white-background ID photo. No criminal record requested.

Revenue caps: 5 million DZD for services, 10 million DZD for trade. Tax rate: 0.5% flat-rate final tax (IFU). Mandatory CASNOS affiliation within 10 days (contributions around 32,000 DZD/year). This status does not allow hiring employees.

Timeline: 2 to 5 days for validation, then card pickup at the post office upon SMS notification (cost: 1,200 DZD). Average total time: 7 to 15 days.

Ideal for: freelancers, consultants, service providers, small online businesses.

## Status 2 — EURL (Single-Member Limited Liability Company)

The EURL is the company form for a sole partner. If you're setting up alone, it's the natural status. The procedures are identical to an SARL and go through the CNRC.

## Status 3 — SARL (Limited Liability Company)

The SARL is for 2 to 50 partners. If you have partners or plan to, choose the SARL directly rather than an EURL to be converted later.

## EURL/SARL procedures via the CNRC

To set up an EURL or SARL, all procedures go through the CNRC (National Trade Register Center).

1. **Reserve the company name** via Sijilcom (CNRC's online platform) — prepare 3 to 4 alternative names.
2. **Draft and authenticate the articles of association** with a notary — cost between 15,000 and 50,000 DZD. Note: the CNRC rejects about 1 in 3 applications for missing clauses in the articles.
3. **Deposit the capital** in a blocked bank account (recommended minimum: 100,000 DZD) — blocking certificate required.
4. **Publication in the BOAL** (Official Bulletin of Legal Notices) — cost between 3,000 and 6,000 DZD.
5. **Registration with the CNRC** — trade register extract issued in 7 to 15 days.
6. **Obtain the NIF** from the Tax Directorate — 48 to 72h.
7. **Obtain the NIS** from the ONS — 2 to 4 days.
8. **Open the business bank account** — the blocked capital is released after obtaining the NIF.

Total EURL/SARL cost: between 150,000 and 300,000 DZD (about €1,000 to €2,000).

## Registered office — mandatory address in Algeria

Every company must have an address in Algeria, physical or virtual.

**Commercial premises**: ideal solution for activities involving client visits or storage.

**Manager's home**: accepted for activities without client visits. Algerian proof of address must be provided.

**Commercial registered-office service**: professional address without physical office, between 2,000 and 8,000 DZD/month in Algiers. Ideal solution for 100% online activities or project owners not yet settled in Algeria.

## Which status to choose?

Alone, revenue < 5M DZD, no employees → ANAE self-employed. Alone, revenue > 5M DZD or need for employees → EURL via CNRC. Multiple partners → SARL via CNRC.

## Frequently asked questions

**Can everything be done remotely?**
For ANAE: 100% online registration, but the card is physically collected at a post office in Algeria. For EURL/SARL: some steps require physical presence or a representative on-site via consular power of attorney.

heriter-bien-immobilier-algerie-france.titre: How to inherit property in Algeria from France: complete 2026 guide
heriter-bien-immobilier-algerie-france.resume: A parent recently passed away in Algeria and you live in France? Here are all the concrete steps to inherit an apartment, house, or land in Algeria.
heriter-bien-immobilier-algerie-france.contenu:
## The applicable law

For any real estate located in Algeria, Algerian law applies mandatorily (lex situs), regardless of your nationality or place of residence. This is confirmed by the French Consulate in Algiers. The estate is governed by Articles 126 to 201 of the Algerian Family Code.

## The Fredha — the central document

The Fredha is the Algerian certificate of inheritance, equivalent to the French certificate of heirship. It is issued by the Algerian notary of the place of residence or burial of the deceased. It designates all heirs and their shares. Without the Fredha, no action on the property is possible.

## Steps from France

**Step 1 — Obtain the Algerian death certificate**

If the death occurred in France, contact the competent Algerian consulate for the declaration procedures and to obtain the certificate.

**Step 2 — Contact an Algerian notary**

The notary draws up the Fredha based on the civil status documents of all heirs. If you cannot travel, give power of attorney to a relative or a lawyer in Algeria.

**Step 3 — Taxation**

There are no inheritance taxes in the strict sense in Algeria. Transfer fees apply when ownership is transferred. In France, if the deceased was a French resident, an estate declaration must be filed within 6 months (12 months if the death occurred abroad). The 1999 France-Algeria treaty avoids double taxation.

**Step 4 — Distribution**

If all heirs agree, a notarized distribution deed is drawn up. In case of disagreement or an untraceable heir, a judicial distribution can be requested from the Algerian court — a lawyer then becomes essential.

**Step 5 — Title transfer**

The notary transfers the property title at the land registry in the name of the new owners.

## Required documents

- Death certificate (translated into Arabic if issued in France)
- Birth certificates of all heirs
- Family record book of the deceased
- Property title if available
- Legalized power of attorney if you appoint a representative

## Difficult situations

**Untitled property**: first regularize the title at the land registry — without an authentic notarized deed, no inheritance is possible.

**Doing nothing**: the estate remains undivided, no heir can sell alone, and the situation becomes more complex with each generation.

## Frequently asked questions

**Do I need to travel to Algeria?**
Not necessarily — a power of attorney to a lawyer or relative is enough for most procedures.

**Are there inheritance taxes in Algeria?**
Not in the strict sense. Only transfer fees when ownership changes.

vendre-appartement-algerie-etranger.titre: How to sell an apartment in Algeria from abroad: complete 2026 guide
vendre-appartement-algerie-etranger.resume: You have an apartment in Algeria and want to sell it from France, Belgium or Canada? Here is the complete, step-by-step guide.
vendre-appartement-algerie-etranger.contenu:
## Can you sell without traveling?

Yes, thanks to consular power of attorney. You appoint a relative or a lawyer in Algeria to sign the deed of sale on your behalf. This power of attorney is drawn up at the Algerian consulate of your city of residence — it is recognized directly by Algerian notaries.

## Prerequisites for the sale

**Valid title deed**: you must have an authentic notarized deed registered at the land registry. Without an authentic title, no legal sale is possible.

**No blocking joint ownership**: if the property is jointly owned, all co-owners or heirs must consent to the sale.

**No outstanding charges**: check at the land registry that there is no mortgage or seizure.

## The steps

**Step 1 — Consular power of attorney**

Go to the Algerian consulate with your Algerian ID. The consulate draws up the power of attorney authorizing your representative to sign all documents. This document is legalized and recognized directly by Algerian notaries.

**Step 2 — Valuation and listing**

Appoint a real estate agent or a lawyer in Algeria to value the property. Always insist on a price 100% declared to the notary — refuse any partial "off the books" payment.

**Step 3 — Preliminary sales agreement**

Your representative signs the preliminary agreement with the buyer. A lawyer can secure this step.

**Step 4 — Final notarized deed**

The deed is signed at the Algerian notary's office by your representative and the buyer. Registration and land publication follow. Time between agreement and deed: 1 to 6 months.

**Step 5 — Fees and taxes**

Notary fees between 2 and 5% of the price. A capital gains tax may apply. If you are a French tax resident, the capital gain may also be taxable in France — consult a tax advisor before selling.

## Repatriating funds

Transfers of dinars from Algeria abroad are regulated by the Bank of Algeria. Non-residents who acquired their property via a legal foreign currency transfer are entitled to repatriate funds in the same currency. For inherited properties or those acquired in dinars, conditions differ. Consult a specialized Algerian lawyer before selling.

## Risks to avoid

Never sell without going through a notary. Only grant power of attorney to someone of absolute trust or a professional lawyer. Refuse any transaction involving part of the price in undeclared cash.

## Frequently asked questions

**How long does a sale take?**
Between 1 and 6 months depending on the complexity of the file.

**Can an inherited property be sold?**
Yes, once the Fredha is established and the property is in your name or jointly owned with the agreement of all heirs.

**Do I need to pay taxes in France?**
Potentially yes if you are a French tax resident. Consult a tax advisor before selling.
